import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class bubblestrike {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
        int N = scanner.nextInt();
        double P = scanner.nextDouble();
        
        int low = 0, high = N;
        while (low < high) {
            int mid = (low + high) / 2;
            if (canAchieveProbability(mid, N, P)) {
                high = mid;
            } else {
                low = mid + 1;
            }
        }
        System.out.println(low);
    }

    private static boolean canAchieveProbability(int good, int total, double required) {
        if (good == 0) {
            return false;
        }
        int bad = total - good;
        
        // Total ways to choose 3 maps from total maps
        long totalWays = (long)total * (total - 1) * (total - 2) / 6;
        if (totalWays == 0) return false;
        
        long favorable = 0;
        
        // Case 1: All 3 maps are good maps
        if (good >= 3) {
            favorable += (long)good * (good - 1) * (good - 2) / 6;
        }
        
        // Case 2: 2 good maps and 1 bad map
        if (good >= 2 && bad >= 1) {
            favorable += (long)good * (good - 1) / 2 * bad;
        }
        
        // Case 3: 1 good map and 2 bad maps
        if (good >= 1 && bad >= 2) {
            favorable += (long)good * bad * (bad - 1) / 2;
        }
        
        // Case 4: 3 bad maps - favorable only if both players discard the same bad map
        // In this case, the system randomly selects one of the 3 maps that weren't picked
        // If both players discard the same map (prob 1/3), then 2 maps remain, system picks randomly (1/2 chance for good)
        // If players discard different maps (prob 2/3), then 1 map remains, system must pick that (1/0 chance for good if it's good)
        // Actually, let's reconsider the problem:
        // - System shows 3 maps
        // - Each player picks one to discard (randomly among 3)
        // - System randomly selects one of the maps not picked by any player
        
        // For 3 bad maps: 
        // - If both players discard the same map (3 ways: both discard map1, both discard map2, both discard map3), 
        //   probability = 3/9 = 1/3, then 2 maps remain, system picks randomly, 0 good maps remain, so 0 chance
        // - If players discard different maps (6 ways), 1 map remains, system picks that, 0 good maps, so 0 chance
        // So 3 bad maps contributes 0 favorable outcomes
        
        // For 2 bad, 1 good:
        // - Both discard same map: 3 ways
        //   * Both discard good: 1 way, 2 bad remain, system picks randomly, 0 good
        //   * Both discard bad: 2 ways, 1 bad + 1 good remain, system picks randomly, 1/2 chance good
        // - Both discard different: 6 ways
        //   * Discard good+bad: 2*2=4 ways (player1 good, player2 bad1 or bad2; player1 bad1, player2 good; etc.)
        //     Actually: player1 has 3 choices, player2 has 3 choices, total 9 combinations
        //     Same discard: (good,good), (bad1,bad1), (bad2,bad2) = 3 ways
        //     Different: 6 ways
        //     For different: if one discards good and one discards bad, 1 map remains (the other bad), system picks it, 0 good
        //     If both discard different bads, 1 map remains (good), system picks it, 1 good
        //     So: (bad1,bad2) and (bad2,bad1) = 2 ways where good remains
        
        // Let's recalculate more carefully:
        // Total combinations: 3*3 = 9 (player1 choice, player2 choice)
        
        // For 1 good (G) and 2 bad (B1, B2):
        // - (G,G): discard G, remain B1,B2, system picks randomly, 0 good
        // - (G,B1): discard G,B1, remain B2, system picks B2, 0 good
        // - (G,B2): discard G,B2, remain B1, system picks B1, 0 good
        // - (B1,G): discard B1,G, remain B2, system picks B2, 0 good
        // - (B1,B1): discard B1, remain G,B2, system picks randomly, 1/2 good
        // - (B1,B2): discard B1,B2, remain G, system picks G, 1 good
        // - (B2,G): discard B2,G, remain B1, system picks B1, 0 good
        // - (B2,B1): discard B2,B1, remain G, system picks G, 1 good
        // - (B2,B2): discard B2, remain G,B1, system picks randomly, 1/2 good
        
        // Favorable: (B1,B1), (B2,B2), (B1,B2), (B2,B1) = 2 + 2 = 4 out of 9
        // Probability = 4/9
        
        // For 2 good (G1, G2) and 1 bad (B):
        // - (G1,G1): discard G1, remain G2,B, system picks randomly, 1/2 good
        // - (G1,G2): discard G1,G2, remain B, system picks B, 0 good
        // - (G1,B): discard G1,B, remain G2, system picks G2, 1 good
        // - (G2,G1): discard G2,G1, remain B, system picks B, 0 good
        // - (G2,G2): discard G2, remain G1,B, system picks randomly, 1/2 good
        // - (G2,B): discard G2,B, remain G1, system picks G1, 1 good
        // - (B,G1): discard B,G1, remain G2, system picks G2, 1 good
        // - (B,G2): discard B,G2, remain G1, system picks G1, 1 good
        // - (B,B): discard B, remain G1,G2, system picks randomly, 1 good
        
        // Favorable: (G1,B), (G2,B), (B,G1), (B,G2), (B,B) = 4 + 1 = 5 out of 9
        // Plus (G1,G1) and (G2,G2) give 1/2 each, so 2 * 1/2 = 1
        // Total favorable = 5 + 1 = 6 out of 9 = 2/3
        
        // For 3 good maps:
        // - Any discard combination leaves at least 1 good map
        // - (G1,G1): remain G2,G3, system picks randomly, 1 good
        // - (G1,G2): remain G3, system picks G3, 1 good
        // - etc.
        // Actually all 9 combinations result in at least 1 good map being selected
        // So probability = 1
        
        // Let's verify with the original formula:
        // favorable = 0.25 * b * (b - 1) + g * (g - 1) * (g - 2) / 6.0 + 0.5 * b * g * (g - 1);
        // This seems to be trying to compute something but let's derive properly
        
        // Actually, let's compute probability directly:
        // P(success) = P(3 good) * 1 + P(2 good, 1 bad) * (5/9 + 2/18) + P(1 good, 2 bad) * (4/9) + P(0 good) * 0
        // Wait, let me recalculate the 2 good 1 bad case more carefully:
        
        // For 2 good (G1,G2) and 1 bad (B):
        // Total combinations: 9
        // Success cases (system picks good):
        // - (G1,G1): remain G2,B, system picks randomly: 1/2 chance good
        // - (G2,G2): remain G1,B, system picks randomly: 1/2 chance good
        // - (G1,B): remain G2, system picks G2: 1 good
        // - (G2,B): remain G1, system picks G1: 1 good
        // - (B,G1): remain G2, system picks G2: 1 good
        // - (B,G2): remain G1, system picks G1: 1 good
        // - (B,B): remain G1,G2, system picks randomly: 1 good
        // - (G1,G2): remain B, system picks B: 0 good
        // - (G2,G1): remain B, system picks B: 0 good
        
        // So: 2*(1/2) + 4*1 + 1*1 + 2*0 = 1 + 4 + 1 = 6 out of 9 = 2/3
        
        // For 1 good (G) and 2 bad (B1,B2):
        // Success cases:
        // - (G,G): remain B1,B2, system picks randomly: 0 good
        // - (G,B1): remain B2, system picks B2: 0 good
        // - (G,B2): remain B1, system picks B1: 0 good
        // - (B1,G): remain B2, system picks B2: 0 good
        // - (B2,G): remain B1, system picks B1: 0 good
        // - (B1,B1): remain G,B2, system picks randomly: 1/2 good
        // - (B2,B2): remain G,B1, system picks randomly: 1/2 good
        // - (B1,B2): remain G, system picks G: 1 good
        // - (B2,B1): remain G, system picks G: 1 good
        
        // So: 2*(1/2) + 2*1 = 1 + 2 = 3 out of 9 = 1/3
        
        // Wait, that's 3/9 = 1/3, not 4/9 as I thought earlier. Let me recount:
        // (B1,B2) and (B2,B1) = 2 cases with 1 good
        // (B1,B1) and (B2,B2) = 2 cases with 1/2 good each = 1 total
        // Total = 2 + 1 = 3 out of 9 = 1/3
        
        // So the probability formula should be:
        // P = C(g,3)/C(n,3) * 1 + C(g,2)*C(b,1)/C(n,3) * (2/3) + C(g,1)*C(b,2)/C(n,3) * (1/3)
        
        long totalCombinations = (long)total * (total - 1) * (total - 2);
        long favorableCases = 0;
        
        // 3 good maps
        if (good >= 3) {
            favorableCases += (long)good * (good - 1) * (good - 2);
        }
        
        // 2 good, 1 bad
        if (good >= 2 && bad >= 1) {
            favorableCases += (long)good * (good - 1) * bad * 2; // 2/3 = 4/6, but we're using total*2 for denominator
        }
        
        // 1 good, 2 bad
        if (good >= 1 && bad >= 2) {
            favorableCases += (long)good * bad * (bad - 1);
        }
        
        // Probability = favorableCases / totalCombinations
        double probability = (double)favorableCases / totalCombinations;
        return probability >= required;
    }
}
